📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two large studies published on November 5 link declining newborn vitamin K shot rates to a sharp increase in infant bleeding cases, including potentially fatal brain hemorrhages.

A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.

In a recent development, A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S. infants, found that refusal rates more than doubled, rising from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Infants who did not receive the shot had a 47% higher risk of bleeding and more than twice the risk of intracranial bleeding.

Additionally, newly introduced data from Truveta suggest the trend is continuing: refusals of vitamin K shots increased by 57% between January and June 2026, rising from 5.2% to 8.1% of newborns.

Sources indicate that vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, and newborns naturally have very low levels. Without the preventive injection, infants are at risk for VKDB, which can cause sudden bleeding in the brain, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs. Late-onset VKDB can occur up to six months after birth, often without warning signs, and may be fatal.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) continue to recommend an intramuscular vitamin K injection for all newborns, ideally within 6 hours of birth.

The shot is not a vaccine; it is a nutrient injection that helps prevent dangerous bleeding. A single dose reduces the risk of late-onset VKDB by approximately 98%.

Experts not involved in the studies attribute the rise in refusals partly to broader vaccine hesitancy and mixed public health messaging.

“The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision,” said Graham Tse, MD, a pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

According to recent reports, some of these factors, Tse said, include conflicting messages from federal health agencies such as the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), both overseen by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., an outspoken critic of the childhood immunization schedule.

It has been revealed that the vitamin K shot is not a vaccine, yet RFK Jr. has declined to reassure parents about its safety, despite the CDC’s current recommendation to administer it at birth.

Additionally, growing medical distrust among parents has led to refusal of routine newborn care, such as the vitamin K shot, Reuters reports.

Healthline spoke with Tse to learn more about the risks of refusing the vitamin K shot and what latest or expectant parents should know about this routine newborn treatment.

This interview has been lightly edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Tse: The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision.

A contributing factor to the decline in vitamin K injection at birth, as well as in newborn hepatitis B vaccination, is the conflicting messages from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Recommendations from these entities and others are conflicting or do not align with established, research-based, and proven recommendations from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Infectious Diseases Society of America.

When there are conflicting recommendations, it creates confusion and doubt among parents about what the best or right choice is for their child.

As well, there is so much misinformation on the internet, among influencers, and on social media that it is difficult to know what information is accurate, well-researched, and proven, versus what may be just someone’s opinion or belief.

Some are mistaking the vitamin K injection at birth for a vaccination, which it is not. Ultimately, all these factors are contributing to parents declining or delaying vitamin K injections at birth.

In a recent development, tse: Declining the newborn vitamin K injection puts the newborn at significant risk of serious and life threatening complications from vitamin K-deficient bleeding (VKDB). This was previously referred to as hemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

VKDB can be as mild as bruising of the skin but can be as serious as bleeding into the brain, and newborns and infants can die from VKDB.

Declining vitamin K injection at birth is significant because of the serious and potentially life threatening consequences of deficiency of Vitamin K and not being able to clot the blood.

The vitamin K injection at birth is highly effective at preventing VKDB.

Tse: If a neonate or infant has vitamin K deficiency, the ability to clot their blood and stop bleeding is highly reduced.

All newborns are at risk of low vitamin K due to low body stores, low vitamin K content of breast milk, reduced ability of the gut to mobilize vitamin K, and poor transfer of vitamin K across the placenta.

When the blood cannot clot, bleeding from minor or minimal trauma can occur, and even bleeding without injury or trauma may occur. This can include bruises, bleeding from the mouth or gastrointestinal tract, bleeding from cuts or circumcision.

Bleeding can occur anywhere in the body, including in the brain, which can be catastrophic.

Sources indicate that VKDB can occur from birth and through several months of life. Bleeding in the brain from VKDB, one of the most serious consequences, can occur at any time from birth to up to 6 months or so and can occur unexpectedly and suddenly. Vitamin K given at birth can prevent this risk of bleeding.

In a recent development, tse: Vitamin K is a necessary vitamin that all humans need. Vitamin K is not a vaccination.

Newborns need vitamin K to prevent serious, significant, and often catastrophic bleeding during their first several months of life.

Vitamin K has been given to newborns in the United States for close to 70 years, is safe, is studied, and is proven to help prevent vitamin K-deficient bleeding.

I urge upcoming parents to allow their newborns to receive the vitamin K injection at birth — it protects them, keeps them healthy, is proven safe, and is recommended.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting newly introduced series concurrent player records on Steam.
  • According to recent reports, the latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting newly introduced series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

According to recent reports, the latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

It has been revealed that battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

It has been revealed that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

Industry observers note that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its new Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-new iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the organization’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the fresh battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the organization is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We mentioned we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A tech giant spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

In a recent development, the 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

According to recent reports, it features BMW’s new “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW mentioned you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW remarked enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

The electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW claims it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Recent findings suggest that inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a latest 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Industry observers note that edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s new iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

Industry observers note that by 2030, BMW looks to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, said.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

#29414. Breaking: Why the Word “Boundaries” Makes Boomer Parents Mad

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1215 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Why the Word “Boundaries” Makes Boomer Parents Mad

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1215 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.
  • When the topic of boundaries comes up, a Millennial woman (born 1981-1996 according to Pew Research) will vigorously nod in agreement.
  • How did a word meant to build healthier relationships become one that is so triggering?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

When the topic of boundaries comes up, a Millennial woman (born 1981-1996 according to Pew Research) will vigorously nod in agreement. But when that same daughter tries to install those boundaries with her Baby Boomer mother, (born between 1946-1964, according to Pew Research), the reaction can be swift and negative: Mom gives a raised eyebrow, a long silence, or an extreme and snarky reply.

How did a word meant to build healthier relationships become one that is so triggering? Why do boundaries make your family members feel rejected? The issue isn't the latest behavior and delineation itself, but what the word signals.

Recent findings suggest that for some adult daughters (Gen X were born 1965-1980; Millennials born 1981-1996; and even adult Gen Z (born 1997-2012, according to Pew Research), boundaries represent a way to honor yourself, not give up on the elements in a relationship that matter to you, and hopefully reflect your evolving emotional maturity. For a Baby Boomer parent, boundary talk sounds like withdrawal, rejection, and pulling away from the family (or particularly from them).

Part of the problem is that the paradigm of “Boomers vs. Millennials” has become a ready-made cultural storyline. In a 2026 study of Instagram memes about the two generations, media researchers Centorrino and Ferrigno found that the largest group of memes did one thing above all: draw lines between generations. That is, sow division between the Millennial and the Boomer. These memes ranged from dismissive jokes like “OK Boomer” to side-by-side comparisons of what each generation was like at the same age, but with a negative twist. The researchers argue that generational labels work less like neutral categories and more like symbolic boundaries, sorting people into “us” and “them.” It can become a crass classification system or a way of saying "they're not like me and my peers.".

With this culturally sensitive division in mind, when a daughter deploys the language of boundaries, her mother may not hear a healthy limit. She may hear one more line being drawn between “your generation” and “mine.” In short, she feels pushed away and made fun of for her behaviors and ways of doing things. That's a pretty significant barrier to hearing their adult child in a neutral or healthy way.

Research on adult development helps explain why this mismatch runs so deep. Karen Fingerman, a leading researcher on parents and adult children, and her colleagues draw on socioemotional selectivity theory. This theory suggests that as people age, they become more invested in keeping their longest-standing close ties than in forming upcoming ones. That means they get really zoned-in on their adult children, their own siblings, and lifelong close friends.

Industry observers note that in a 2024 study of more than 300 adults aged 65 and older, Fingerman’s team found that nearly three-quarters of participants’ long-term relationships were with family. That means most of what an older person wants is from their adult kids. They're invested in these long-term relationships with a deep intensity. However, the parent-child ties were also complicated. The time older folks spent with their family members was linked to more stressful conversations and intense moods (both positive and negative). All this means that Boomer parents are putting an intense lens on their adult child and it's kind of stressful.

In a recent development, and here's the rub. That intensity only goes one way. Researchers have described the concept of “intergenerational stake”: parents tend to be more invested in their children than children are in their parents. In a 2015 study of more than 600 middle-aged adults, Kira Birditt, Fingerman, and colleagues found that people rated their relationships with their children as both more vital and more negative than their relationships with their own parents. Friction, in other words, can be a sign of how much a relationship matters. In sum, the more an adult child matters to their parent, the more likely there's tension as they seek connection.

Why does that friction occur? Fingerman’s earlier work points to an answer. In a 1996 study of 48 mothers over 70 and their middle-aged daughters, she introduced the term “developmental schism” to describe tension that arises because mothers and daughters are at different points in adult development. That's the sandpaper feeling between mothers and adult daughters, even when there's a lot of love. Two of the biggest sources of that tension were independence and how much importance each person places on the relationship. Many of today’s Boomer mothers were once the daughters in research like this, navigating the same tug-of-war with their own mothers. They haven't forgotten that. They're trying to discern how to manage things well with their own daughters, but sometimes it still comes off poorly.

According to recent reports, that is the boundary conversation in a nutshell. A daughter may be focused on protecting her time, energy, and independence. Her mother is at a stage of life when she is intensely focused on family ties. She's laser-focused on keeping the relationship close, but maybe doesn't have the skills to make it happen, just the desire for it to be so. Both daughter and mother are responding to real needs. They just aren’t the same needs.

And nowhere does that mismatch become more visible than during the holidays, when traditions, expectations, and family identities are on full display.

As a family communication researcher, I’ve spent more than a decade studying the invisible work of daughtering: the task, emotional, cognitive, and identity labor adult daughters do to keep families connected. Lately, I’ve become especially interested in what happens when daughters begin to renegotiate that work.

Boundary conflict isn’t really about what a daughter is willing to do or a wall she's putting in place with her mother. The tension is about what these boundaries end up meaning to everyone else. A daughter's work (or lack thereof) ripples to every corner of the family. When she decides to prioritize some needs more than others and set down some of the unnecessary labor she's been doing, expect the family to shift, either seismically or gently, but it will change nonetheless. But you should know, daughter, you have every right not to abandon yourself and your needs. Set the boundary, but don't be shocked when others dislike it or feel hurt. Wait it out with empathy and gentle understanding. A latest paradigm is on the horizon.

According to recent reports, centorrino, M., & Ferrigno, C. (2026). Memetic narratives of generational conflict: The “boomers vs. millennials” frame on Instagram. Journalism and Media, 7(3), 187. https://www.mdpi.com/2673-5172/7/3/187.

Birditt, K. S., Hartnett, C. S., Fingerman, K. L., Zarit, S., & Antonucci, T. C. (2015). Extending the intergenerational stake hypothesis: Evidence of an intraindividual stake and implications for well-being. Journal of Marriage and Family, 77(4), 877–888. https://doi.org/10.1111/jomf.12203.

In a recent development, fingerman, K. L. (1996). Sources of tension in the aging mother and adult daughter relationship. Psychology and Aging, 11(4), 591–606. https://doi.org/10.1037/0882-7974.11.4.591.

Sources indicate that fingerman, K. L., Zhou, Z., Huo, M., Luong, G., & Birditt, K. S. (2024). Enduring bonds: Duration and contact in close relationships in late life. The Gerontologist, 64(4), gnad091. https://doi.org/10.1093/geront/gnad091.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when the mid-engine C111 sports-car concept made its debut at the Frankfurt auto show in 1969, would-be buyers sent blank checks to Mercedes-Benz headquarters. Despite the fervent interest, however, the C111 never went into production, although a handful of prototypes were built over the years. Now Mercedes-Benz has unveiled that it will auction off one of those cars, making it (at long last) the first C111 to reach private hands. And would-be buyers who wish to take home the C111 will need to muster that same blank-check energy.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 14202.

The C111 was conceived as the modern-day successor to the W198 300SL Gullwing of the 1950s. The two-seat supercar featured a mid-mounted rotary engine, a fiberglass body, and gullwing doors. The following year, an evolved C111-II was unveiled at the 1970 Geneva auto show with a 345-hp 2.4-liter four-rotor engine. The 1973 global oil embargo and the costs to meet rising emissions standards caused the organization to shelve the blueprint for series production, although several more C111 prototypes were made, including a C111-II-D with a diesel engine in 1976 and a diesel-powered C111-III in 1978. A total of 17 cars were made; 13 still exist. Mercedes has kept them all, until now.

The car being sold is a C111-II built in August 1970. It’s fitted with a 2.4-liter rotary engine making 345 horsepower at 7700 rpm, a five-speed manual transmission, anti-lock brakes, twin fuel tanks, and a Becker Europa radio. Weighing 2734 pounds, the C111-II had a claimed top speed of 186 mph and a 0-to-60-mph time of 4.8 seconds. It was used as a test car, including at the Hockenheimring.

It has been revealed that like most of the C111s, this car is painted Weissherbst orange; the seats are upholstered in houndstooth fabric. The car sits on modern 8-x-15-inch alloy wheels; the original magnesium wheels from 1970 are included, but with the caveat that they “are now suitable only for display purposes.” The anti-lock brake system is not functional.

Industry observers note that the car has been on display at the Mercedes-Benz Museum since 2006. It was sympathetically restored in 2024 in preparation for an appearance at Pebble Beach. The odometer shows 24,766 km (15,389 miles).

Sources indicate that the car is being auctioned by RM Sotheby’s this coming February in Paris. The proceeds of the sale will help fund the museum, including an initiative to digitize its contents, part of the “Mercedes-Benz Museum 2.0” project.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 14202.

To reassure the future buyer that the value of their C111 won’t be diluted by additional examples coming onto the market, Mercedes-Benz has committed to a 25-year moratorium on any future sales of the remaining cars. Mercedes-Benz collectors, call your bankers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 owners have a newly introduced symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.
  • The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) declared on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 owners have a newly introduced symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) declared on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint stated.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

It has been revealed that the study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

Industry observers note that in a 2024 podcast, Rizzo mentioned he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

Sources indicate that about 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 users “challenging” to interpret.

Across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint noted patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint said that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

As of publication, the FDA’s online label database did not yet show the fresh warning on the drugs’ labels.

#29408. How Hugs Help Combat Anxiety and Pain

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

How Hugs Help Combat Anxiety and Pain

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.
  • Psychological research has shown that hugs can positively affect both physical and mental well-being (Ocklenburg, 2024).
  • According to recent reports, A upcoming study, just published in the Journal of Integrative and Complementary Medicine, aimed to answer exactly this question (Aydın and co-workers, 2026).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.

Psychological research has shown that hugs can positively affect both physical and mental well-being (Ocklenburg, 2024). For example, they have been shown to reduce stress, increase bonding between people, and are associated with reduced feelings of loneliness and depression. One question, however, that has not been answered yet in psychological research is whether hugs can combat anxiety and pain.

According to recent reports, A upcoming study, just published in the Journal of Integrative and Complementary Medicine, aimed to answer exactly this question (Aydın and co-workers, 2026). The study entitled “Preoperative Family Hugging: Associations with Anxiety and Postoperative Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial” was a randomized controlled trial. This is a strong form of scientific experiment in which volunteers are randomly assigned to two groups that are compared. In this study, 150 patients who were about to undergo surgery were randomly assigned to a hug or a no-hug group. Patients in the hug group were instructed to hug family members for at least 20 seconds about 30 minutes before the start of the surgery. Patients in the other group did not hug anyone.

Sources indicate that about 30 minutes later, patients’ anxiety was measured in the operating room using standard anxiety questionnaires. Afterward, patients in both groups were anesthetized, and surgery was performed. After they woke up again, their pain levels were assessed using standard pain questionnaires 30 minutes and 6 hours after surgery.

The results of the study revealed a clear and statistically significant difference in state anxiety before surgery between the groups. Patients in the hugging group reported lower anxiety before surgery than patients who did not hug anyone before the surgery. Further analyses also highlighted that the patients in the hugging group showed lower pain levels after surgery than patients who did not hug before the surgery. Six hours after surgery, no pain differences were found between the groups.

As the randomized controlled trial is a strong form of experiment, these results can be interpreted as a sign that hugs indeed may help reduce pain and anxiety in the context of surgery. While more psychological experiments are needed to explain this effect, one idea could be that the bonding hormone oxytocin could play a role. Hugs have been known to lead to oxytocin release, and oxytocin has been known to interact with the pain system and the function of the amygdala, a central brain area for feelings of anxiety and fear.

Sources indicate that the study shows strong empirical evidence that a hug before surgery can help reduce anxiety and pain. So, the next time you visit a loved one in the hospital: Hug them!

Aydın A, Kutlusoy S, Gökdere OG. Preoperative Family Hugging: Associations with Anxiety and Postoperative Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial. Journal of Integrative and Complementary Medicine. 2026;0(0). doi:10.1177/27683605261505158.

Ocklenburg, S. (2024). The Psychology and Neuroscience of Hugging. A Multidisciplinary Perspective. Springer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

It has been revealed that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Industry observers note that coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios claims the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

It has been revealed that as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

In a recent development, so far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The upcoming BMW M3 EV sports sedan represents BMW's biggest attempt to woo electric-car buyers to date. The maker's first inception-to-showroom production electric M car carries styling derived from the standard i3, but with M-specific fender bulges, aero enhancements, and racier-looking exterior lighting elements. BMW notes the M3 EV will coexist with a gasoline-powered M3, which should arrive in showrooms ahead of the electric model.

Sources indicate that like the i3 and BMW's other Neue Klasse models, the M3 EV features an 800-volt architecture and batteries that offer 20 percent higher energy density than past EVs. BMW M vehicles have cultivated a devoted following for their sublime performance, and it stands to reason that BMW wouldn't risk tainting that legacy when the power comes from electrons instead of gasoline.

Expert Tip: If you can't wait for the M3 EV to launch before deciding on your next BMW sports sedan, consider the outgoing i4, which is one of our favorite EVs and can be had with a 592-hp dual-motor powertrain.

Recent findings suggest that everything. Details are scarce, but we know the M3 will ride atop BMW's newly introduced EV platform. Production is expected to begin sometime in 2027.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

It has been revealed that the M3 EV will be powered by four electric motors producing a total of 838 horsepower and 885 pound-feet of torque. The motors themselves are of the electrically excited variety, and the quad-motor setup allows for torque vectoring both front to back and side to side. The car operates in rear-wheel-drive mode most of the time, with the front motors coming online when needed.

It has been revealed that the M3 EV utilizes BMW's "Heart of Joy" control unit and software, which handles the drivetrain, braking, charging, regeneration, and steering functions. When we drove a prototype of the electric M3, we found it to be a beast on the racetrack. We also experimented with the different drive modes, including the fake gearshifts and sounds in the various eDrive settings, but thought the car was best in Auto mode.

Recent findings suggest that BMW indicates the electric M3 will come with a battery pack measuring roughly 100 kilowatt-hours. This should provide an EPA-rated driving range of around 300 miles, though we’re still awaiting official EPA estimates. DC fast-charging capability is said to be up to 420 kilowatts, which should enable the M3 to add a considerable amount of range in a short period of time.

In a recent development, first Row: Like the i3, the M3 EV features BMW's latest digital dashboard, which features a trapezoidal infotainment display. The concept car pictured here indicates deeply bucketed performance seats with five-point safety harnesses, but expect normal chairs and seatbelts on the production model. The concept vehicle also demonstrated a cloth trim piece on the dashboard with multi-colored ambient backlighting.

Second Row: A pair of bucket seats was shown in the concept vehicle, although we think a three-across bench will at least be offered on the production M3 EV.

Cargo Capacity: We aren't sure about the M3 EV's cargo capacity yet, but we expect to see storage in both the trunk and the front trunk.

The touchscreen offers a high level of customization and features a matrix backlight for easy visibility in all conditions. BMW's new Panoramic Vision system projects crucial information onto the lower part of the windshield, stretching from A-pillar to A-pillar. Logically, key driving information is displayed on the left for the driver, while central and right-hand areas of the display can be personalized and are visible to all occupants.

Up to six widgets can be moved from the infotainment screen to the Panoramic Vision system by drag and drop, and further customization of both screens can be manipulated by buttons on the steering wheel. A head-up display is available, and smartphones and smartwatches from all leading manufacturers can be programmed to operate as the vehicle key.

In a recent development, if your domicile happens to exist, say, under a large boulder, you might not have heard that Grand Theft Auto VI is finally arriving at the stroke of midnight on November 19. Those of us who watch television, browse the web, scroll social media, listen to the radio, read the newspaper, flip through magazines, or consume outside info in any way are well aware of the video game, however. It’s the latest installment of the immensely popular “Grand Theft Auto” series, which combines a (surprisingly deep) vein of car culture with an immersive open world full of theft, fighting, drugs, and other violent delights.

While the previous games came out on a semi-regular schedule of one every few years, it’s been 13 trips ‘round the sun since the last one hit stores. (GTA VI’s development has been so delayed, it even inspired a meme.) Suffice it to say, there’s a lot of pent-up anticipation—even enough to spark half-founded panic headlines about millions of people around the world call in sick to play. But there’s another report that puts a bit more solid of a figure on the excitement around the game. According to digital analysis firm SensorTower, GTA VI has already racked up $1.65 billion in pre-sales ahead of its launch.

That correlates to a little over 17 million orders for the game so far, according to the report, with 75 percent of pre-sales going for the PlayStation 5 version and the other 25 percent for Xbox Series X|S consoles. The chart highlights a fairly typical exponential curve growth over the last five months since pre-sales kicked off: a long period of incremental gains, followed by rapid acceleration in the last few weeks.

And GTA VI-based revenue seems likely to keep coming in to creator Rockstar Games’s coffers at quite a clip, considering initial reviews for the game have been stellar so far. While it may not be your typical automotive-themed driving game, the latest release seems all but sure to guarantee Grand Theft Auto remains a serious part of car culture for some time to come.

Juiced Scrambler Mini rolled out as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.
  • In a recent development, the new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable company. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

In a recent development, the new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

In a recent development, the Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

According to recent reports, that setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may rapidly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

In a recent development, there’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

It has been revealed that the bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

The Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is presently offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The organization claims preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

Recent findings suggest that that price also comes with something increasingly important in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual firm standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, promptly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

Recent findings suggest that there’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

When it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

According to recent reports, it’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real firm standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

Latest Update: Why Do I Have to Do Everything?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.
  • Every relationship has its own way of giving and receiving.
  • Industry observers note that sometimes these differences create a power imbalance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.

Every relationship has its own way of giving and receiving. Partners contribute their money, time, emotional and logistical support, and domestic labor, among other activities and resources. Both give, and both take. But it’s rare that both people contribute equally in all these domains. In other words, in most categories, one person is doing more than the other. Often, one partner ends up feeling angry that they are “doing it all” in the sphere of their focus.

Industry observers note that sometimes these differences create a power imbalance. For example, if one person earns significantly more than the other, this can subtly influence how the couple makes a large financial decision. The person who earns less may feel less entitled to their opinions, needs, or wants. They may feel less autonomy. They may also feel an obligation to reciprocate in other ways, even if it’s unspoken. As for the person who contributes more, their role may create a feeling of burden or over-responsibility. This can lead to feelings of resentment or burnout.

People in intimate relationships may try to rectify or avoid these pitfalls by attempting to make every contribution equal. But given that equal contribution in all spheres is virtually impossible, perhaps avoiding pitfalls needs to entail something other than that. Perhaps the focus needs to be on seeing the system as a whole and evaluating the contribution each makes within it. In other words, one person may earn more, but the other may provide more logistical support or domestic labor. In this way, there may be differences in the spheres of contribution, but as a whole, each partner may feel the arrangement is fair.

According to recent reports, furthermore, it’s crucial that regardless of how much each person contributes, both partners’ decision-making authority, financial independence, and freedom from indebtedness be protected. In other words, just because one partner spends more time on child-rearing, it doesn’t mean the other shouldn’t have an equal say in where that child attends school. And just because one partner earns more money doesn’t mean they should have more authority over how the couple spends it. Of course, the person who carries more responsibility in a particular area may have more expertise or experience, and that deserves consideration. But having more expertise isn’t the same as having more power.

Equality in romantic relationships doesn’t necessarily mean contributing equal amounts of money, time, or labor. It means ensuring that differences in contribution don’t become differences in autonomy, dignity, or power. The goal isn’t to contribute equally to a relationship, but to be aware of all the contributions in all aspects of a shared life. And to recognize that fairness doesn’t necessarily mean equality of contribution. What matters is making sure neither partner’s contribution gives them more ownership of the other person’s life or shared life decisions.

Tech Report: 1 in 3 Infants Diagnosed With Peanut Allergy May Not Have the Condition

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, fresh research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, fresh research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

Industry observers note that researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

According to recent reports, among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, Newly introduced York, said these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

Banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more quickly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s notable for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she mentioned.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

According to recent reports, “The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, our friend Max has his heart set on a Saab.
  • Take the Swedish maker’s fresh-for-1991 900S convertible.
  • In a recent development, the new 900S convertible is the “affordable” Saab droptop; it lists for $28,712, no sin tax necessary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the August 1991 concern of Car and Driver.

In a recent development, our friend Max has his heart set on a Saab. His brother Pete has a Saab with more than 100,000 miles on it, and Max swears the thing is still as tight as one of Madonna’s bustiers. Max also states—having read the brochures—that all Saabs now come with more standard equipment than a fire truck. “Seems to me,” says Max, “that no other car gives you as much quality and stuff for the money.”.

Take the Swedish maker’s fresh-for-1991 900S convertible. You’ll note the absence of the word “Turbo” in that moniker. Previously, Saab’s only ragtop was the sprightly turbocharged edition—as nice a convertible as you’ll find, to be sure, but currently saddled with a $33,712 stick­er. Oh, and that price busts the $30K luxu­ry-tax barrier, so remember to add another $371 to the bottom line for Uncle Sam.

In a recent development, the new 900S convertible is the “affordable” Saab droptop; it lists for $28,712, no sin tax necessary. Of course, you have to give up something to save $5000-plus. That something is performance. Rather than the Turbo’s 160-horsepow­er 2.0-liter four, the 900S uses a new nor­mally aspirated, twin-cam, sixteen-valve 2.1-liter four-banger that produces 140 horsepower at 6000 rpm and 133 pound­-feet of torque at 2900. (For ’91, this engine is standard in all non-turbo 900 models.) Performance with this powerplant is modest—a run to 60 mph takes 9.6 sec­onds—but that doesn't seem to bother Max. “Hey,” he claims, “not everybody wants to be Ayrton Senna.” In its favor, the engine revs smoothly, with a characteristic Saab whine, and delivers good fuel economy. Our test car turned in a 24-mpg average.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

Sources indicate that the rest of the car is a near copy of the Turbo convertible. Which is to say, the 900S is one of the most satisfying sun cars around. The cloth top is power-operated; lowering it is as easy as unlocking two headliner latches and pushing a console­mounted button. With the top down, the body is tight and all but shake-free. Saab attributes the body’s rigidity to its pedigree: the droptop 900S is not a beheaded coupe but a designed-from-the-ground-up soft-top built on a dedicated production line.

Industry observers note that as Max has rightly discovered, Saabs justify their sticker prices by being very well equipped. Included in the convertible’s $28,712 base price is everything a discern­ing driver is likely to want: a driver-side air bag; anti-lock brakes; leather seats; power windows, locks, and mirrors; a potent AM/FM/cassette stereo; fog lights; and a headlight wiper/washer system.

According to recent reports, if the Saab’s price seems steep com­pared with such convertibles as the Chrysler LeBaron, the Olds Cutlass Supreme, or even the Mazda Miata, bear in mind that few buyers considering the Saab are likely to have those cars on their potential-purchases list. The 900S’s real competitors are such prestige sunsters as the BMW 325i, the Infiniti M30, and even the Cadillac Allanté. The 900S sells for substantially less than all of those, yet it’s on par in terms of refinement, luxury, solidity, and cachet.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011.

For once, it seems Max has made a decision we can’t argue with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Woodland version is bigger and more powerful than the standard Toyota bZ, and it may be a better deal right now.

Toyota now sells three electric SUVs in the US (see which one is the best fit for you): the bZ (previously called the bZ4Z), C-HR, and bZ Woodland.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is at the moment offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

The deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota noted that if you finance a new 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

In comparison, the standard 2026 bZ is available with 1.99% interest for 72 months at $14.75 for every $1,000 financed.

According to recent reports, for leasing, the standard 2026 Toyota bZ is cheaper, starting at $369 per month. The deal is for a 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing for an effective cost of $490 per month.

In a recent development, however, that’s for the single-motor FWD version. Upgrading to AWD will cost around $606 a month for the same 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing.

Toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

Toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

It has been revealed that in comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

Tested: 2027 Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid Is a Fuel-Economy-Hero Of a Soft-Roader

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability.
  • Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim.
  • Our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability. So it should be no surprise that its Wilderness line of slightly more capable crossovers has been a hit. So, too, has Subaru’s integration of hybrid systems, in an era when buyers of volume cars such as the Forester are happy to get their hands on anything that means greater efficiency.

Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim. The recipe seems like a sales hit waiting to happen, but is it worth the extra complexity?

Our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

According to recent reports, subaru finally brought a hybrid powertrain to the Forester for the 2025 model year. A new Wilderness was introduced a few months later, but it lacked the gas-electric system available on the basic car. The Forester Wilderness Hybrid combines the two, allowing Subaru to offer a system peak of 194 horsepower from a 2.5-liter flat-four and a 1-kWh battery pack.

EPA-estimated fuel economy is down slightly from the basic Forester Hybrid, but the 33 mpg city and 29 mpg highway are still both solid numbers for a crossover with 9.3 inches of ground clearance and Yokohama Geolander all-terrain tires. For most buyers, that improvement alone should justify the price, which is $1000 more than the basic Forester Wilderness.

Powertrain: 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle flat-four, lithium-ion hydride battery pack.

Power: 194 hp @ 5600 rpm (peak system output).

Transmission: continuously variable automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA mpg: 33 city, 29 highway, 31 combined.

In a recent development, befitting the Wilderness Hybrid’s soft-roader credentials, the media drive took place on the dirt, grass, and gravel roads of a private ranch. While this made for beautiful scenery, it did little to showcase what the car could do as a daily driver or challenge its off-road capabilities.

Sources indicate that those capabilities did impress on a more technical off-roading course that Subaru built for the event, although that comes with the caveat that the tech giant presumably built the course with the car’s limits in mind. Even though this is ultimately still a relatively conventional crossover with nothing like the articulation of a more extreme off-roader, the all-terrain tires were capable of handling substantial ruts and steep hill descents.

Approach, break-over, and departure angles of 23.5, 20.6, and 25.5 degrees, respectively, are identical to the nonhybrid Forester Wilderness. This hybrid crossover has the clearance to get over obstacles a car camper or kayaker might find on the trail to their favorite outdoor-recreation spot. The biggest frustration here was the low resolution of the X-Drive off-road menus built into the infotainment screens, a feature that felt behind the respectable capabilities of the crossover itself.

According to recent reports, while the off-road performance is what sets the Wilderness apart from its more pedestrian Forester Hybrid brethren, limited on-road testing suggests that the car feels similar in everyday situations. Given the all-terrain tires, that’s a solid achievement, even if the end result is still relative mediocrity. This Forester is no performance car, and anyone who might have been expecting a canyon carver will instead have to make do with relaxed acceleration and a frustrating continuously variable automatic transmission.

The Forester is a tentpole for Subaru because it combines the basic compact-crossover shape today’s buyers want with some degree of utility in all forms. The Wilderness goes one step further in providing even more capability, but its day-to-day strength will be how little it sacrifices to do that.

The Forester Wilderness Hybrid drops 5 mpg of efficiency in the city in comparison to the standard Forester Hybrid, for 33 mpg. The basic Forester Wilderness, by contrast, gets just 24 mpg in the city. The hybrid remains relatively comfortable and quiet on the road too, which is great news for buyers who do not want to hear harsh noises from all-terrain tires and the unique drone of a Subaru boxer engine all day.

Still, the Wilderness line is differentiated by its capabilities. Buyers looking for a soft-roader do expect to use the car on a trail every so often, which makes the Wilderness Hybrid’s lack of a spare tire a major issue. Since components of the hybrid system are packed where a spare would go on a normal Wilderness, buyers of this car will either have to find another way to carry a fifth tire or contend with the reality that a flat could derail their outdoor adventures in a worse way than the same problem would in the nonhybrid model.

That missing spare tire is one of two major drawbacks for the Wilderness Hybrid. The other is the towing capacity, down from 3500 pounds to just 1500. Both of these are serious limitations for buyers who have certain use cases in mind for their soft-roader, but neither is necessarily a problem for the average buyer. The price difference is not negligible, but fuel savings should cover the difference in cost within a few years. For most buyers, that makes the Hybrid the obvious choice.

Buyers looking at other hybrid soft-roaders could also consider the new Toyota RAV4 Woodland and the Honda CR-V Trailsport. The Subaru is the only one of the three hybrids with conventional full-time all-wheel drive, although that specific differentiator is not necessarily a game changer for buyers who will be spending most of their time on the street. For those who do need to venture a little further a little more often, though, the Forester Hybrid Wilderness seems like the strongest choice.

It has been revealed that subaru’s Wilderness models are sold with synthetic StarTex interiors meant to be easily cleaned, and this particular vehicle even includes a synthetic steering-wheel cover in lieu of the usual leather. This is a small detail for most, but it does mean that the cabin is entirely vegan. For some very specific buyers, however, that one detail could make all the difference.
